If your parents or theirs are against the union, do not go ahead, and do not make your parents your enemies because of an outsider. Instead, seek God’s face in earnest and keep appealing for their understanding. Your marriage needs your parents’ blessing! If your parents are expressing certain concerns, don’t take them lightly; think deeply about what they are saying. Also, do not rush to become part of a family that you are not welcomed into. If your presence is going to tear that family apart, give them peace with your absence. And do not encourage a potential spouse to become enemies with their family because of you. Encourage them to work at being on the same page with their family first. If the marriage can’t wait, you are with the wrong person. Sometimes, what life is telling you through these setbacks is to ‘look before you leap.’ Go into that marriage only after your families have given their blessings. Marriage is one journey that you should not embark on by accumulating bad blood, because half of the success you are going to experience along the way will be decided by your good standing with families from both sides. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources The reality of marriage is rarely ‘me and my spouse only.’ Marriage just finds a way to get others involved in your affairs. And it had better not be people who have never accepted you who will wield significant influence over your spouse! Take seriously the kind of relationship that exists between your partner and their own family (especially their parents). If you are from a close-knit family and you end up marrying someone who is coming from a disunited family, your closeness to your family will become a threat to them. Sometimes, when people mirror certain realities that are lacking in our lives, they trigger us. So, don’t expect someone who is not coming from harmony to extend that energy to your own people. Most likely, they will isolate themselves. May God help you for trying to make them become close to your people! In fact, you will be very lucky if your closeness to your people doesn’t cause rifts in that marriage. So, if maintaining that energy of ‘one family’ is very important to you, look deeply into the family dynamics of your partner’s background. It is not always ‘wickedness’ that keeps people from cultivating a wholesome relationship with in-laws. A lot of times, they don’t know how to flow in the energy they never experienced. And if you force it, it will overwhelm them. My marriage… With Pastor Lukmon George Creating partnership in marriage through encouragement Coscharis boss Maduka pays tribute to wife five years after death Again, constantly being in spaces that are rife with emotional expressions like “I love you” or “I miss you” can either trigger or influence people, though the former is more common than the latter. Please go into marriage with the mindset that your own family (parents, siblings or close relations) are an armour against oppression and other unforeseeable settings. Therefore, be mindful of how you portray them before a spouse and in-laws. The biggest trick of a new marriage is giving the impression that “there will be no problems at all”, but I am here to tell you that problems (both imaginable and unimaginable) will arise down the line, but everything will also depend on how you manage those problems. It is marriage that will teach you that no weapon is stronger than a family that is solidly behind you if you are ever unfortunate to end up with an unreasonable spouse or in-laws. The mistake of most people is putting their loved ones on the butcher’s table before a spouse in a bid to bond with that spouse. But this attitude has consequences that only time will make you experience in full. When people complain about certain inconsideration or disrespectful disposition from an in-law, I usually tell them that the problem is with the ‘see finish’ album of family, which their own relationship has opened for a spouse. It is wisdom to understand that there are 1,001 ways to cultivate and nurture marital intimacy without throwing your family and friends under the bus. You are finished in the hands of a spouse who has zero regard for your loved ones. Marriage will always give you reasons to need your own people! Of course, there are times when it’s one’s own people who do not know how to carry themselves well before their in-laws, but let that be their problem. Just don’t be the one who paints your own people in a bad light before a spouse. When it backfires, you will be more scathed than those you have thrown under the bus. Portraying your people in a bad light before your spouse ends up being a fatal shot on one’s own leg when the chips are down. Chukwuneta Oby
